public.entry.bleqq.origin: noun, from the Swedish word bläck, ink
public.entry.bleqq.deck: One inventory of your bank's obligations.
public.entry.demo.sense1: The real screens of Compliance Watch, opened with a made-up bank inside them.
public.entry.demo.sense2: The quickest way to judge the product, because you can read a briefing, open an obligation and sign a change off before you talk to anyone.
public.entry.spreadsheet.sense1: A table of obligations in which the earlier wording of an edited cell
public.entry.spreadsheet.sense1Pen: stays readable, with the dates it applied.
public.entry.spreadsheet.sense2: A place where a status of compliant
public.entry.spreadsheet.sense2Struck: is one word in a cell
public.entry.spreadsheet.sense2Pen: carries a name, the evidence and a second signature.
public.entry.inbox.sense1: A view of regulatory news that holds
public.entry.inbox.sense1Pen: what a fixed list of sources published, checked on a schedule.
public.entry.watch.sense1: To check each regulator and law gazette on a schedule, in the language it publishes in.
public.entry.watch.sense2: To file what was found as a proposal, which a second agent with its own key confirms against the source before the library changes.
public.entry.watch.usage: Watch sighted the amendment at the six o'clock check and filed it as a proposal.
public.entry.inventory.sense1: Every obligation your bank holds, where each one keeps all its versions and the dates they took effect.
public.entry.inventory.sense2: A record that shows a change sentence by sentence against the wording it replaced, so the earlier text stays readable.
public.entry.inventory.sheetText1: A creditor shall assess the consumer's ability to repay before credit is granted or a credit limit is raised. The assessment shall be based on
public.entry.inventory.sheetText2: information about the consumer's income, expenses and existing debts, and the creditor shall document
public.entry.inventory.sheetIns2: it and keep the record for five years.
public.entry.ask.sense1: To put a question to the inventory and receive an answer with citations to the provisions it came from.
public.entry.ask.sense2: To be told where a change is pending and where the inventory has a gap, in place of a guess.
public.entry.evidence.sense1: The applicability and compliance status of an obligation, recorded for each legal entity with an owner and a date.
public.entry.evidence.sense2: Your bank's own file, private to your zone and kept apart from other banks by row-level security in the database.
public.entry.evidence.usage: The reviewer asked for the evidence, and it carried two names.
public.entry.signOff.sense1: To close a change with a second signature. It is the last of six steps, and every change takes them in this order.
public.entry.signOff.sighted.name: Sighted
public.entry.signOff.sighted.body: by an agent, at the next scheduled check
public.entry.signOff.proposed.name: Proposed
public.entry.signOff.proposed.body: by the agent, against the wording in force
public.entry.signOff.confirmed.name: Confirmed
public.entry.signOff.confirmed.body: by a second agent with its own key
public.entry.signOff.applied.name: Applied
public.entry.signOff.applied.body: to the library, where the old version stays readable
public.entry.signOff.assessed.name: Assessed
public.entry.signOff.assessed.body: by your bank, which decides whether and how it applies
public.entry.signOff.signedOff.name: Signed off
public.entry.signOff.signedOff.body: by a second person in your bank
public.entry.source.sense1: A regulator or law gazette that agents check for your bank. The list is part of the record, so you can show a reviewer what was covered.

public.zones.library.body: The library holds regulations, provisions, obligations and their effective dates, each linked to its source. Every bank reads the same library, so a correction reaches all of them at once.
public.zones.yours.body: Applicability, compliance status, gaps, evidence and sign-off belong to your bank and are never visible outside it.
public.zones.footnote: Your bank's content is kept out of logs and error reports. We send none of it to a model apart from the questions your people type into Ask and what your bank asks its own agents to research, and your bank can switch both off.

public.assurance.title: What your vendor review will ask
public.assurance.access.body: Passkeys are the only way in, so there is no password to phish and no reset link to intercept.
public.assurance.fourEyes.body: Approvals, sign-off and changes to your scope need a second person, and the database refuses the same person in both roles rather than flagging it afterwards.
public.assurance.isolation.body: Row-level security in the database keeps each bank's data out of every other bank's reach, whatever the query.
public.assurance.models.body: Every model call is logged, and content fetched from the web is treated as material to read, never as an instruction to follow.
public.assurance.ledger.body: Every change is stored beside the version it replaced, and its audit entry is written in the same transaction.
public.assurance.retention.body: A record is deleted in full ten years after it was last used.
public.assurance.leaving.body: Two people approve the exit, your bank's data becomes read-only while the final export is taken, and then every row is deleted, including the audit trail.
public.assurance.pack.body: Compliance Watch is an ICT third-party service under DORA, and the pack covers what that brings: the sub-processor register with locations, data flows for each zone, recovery objectives, the incident runbook and the exit plan.
public.questions.ai.a: Agents find changes and file drafts of them as proposals, but they decide nothing for your bank. A fact that a second agent confirms is labelled as machine-confirmed, and what it means for you is decided by your people.
public.questions.oneEntity.q: Can we start with one legal entity?
public.questions.oneEntity.a: You can, and widening the scope later is a request that a second person approves, with both steps recorded.
public.questions.whoSees.a: Only your own people see them. The shared library holds public facts, and your assessments stay in your zone.
public.questions.libraryWrong.q: What if the library is wrong?
public.questions.libraryWrong.a: Report it on the record, and the report stays inside your bank. The agents check each library record against its source on every run and correct it through an ordinary proposal.
public.questions.getIn.a: Your administrator sends an invitation, and each person registers a passkey on their own device. There is no password to set.
public.questions.cost.a: Pricing is agreed with each bank when access is arranged.
public.request.title: Access is by invitation.
public.request.invited: If your bank already uses bleqq, your administrator sends the invitation.
